analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is unsafe object-type dispatch in pre-R13 cleanup: free_preR13_object() calls dwg_free_BLOCK() for objects with fixedtype/type interpreted as BLOCK without validating that the embedded BLOCK fields (notably dynamic pointers like name/xref_pname) were actually initialized to valid heap allocations. With malformed DXF input, a BLOCK object can carry corrupted/non-owned pointer values, and dwg_free_BLOCK_private eventually calls free() on a wild pointer, causing the ASan wild-address write during deallocation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger path is llvmfuzz -> dwg_read_dxf() on attacker-controlled DXF-like bytes (this PoC goes through the DXF branch), producing a malformed pre-R13 BLOCK object state. During final dwg_free(), dwg_free_object() routes pre-R13 objects to free_preR13_object(), which dispatches to dwg_free_BLOCK(); the generated free routine frees BLOCK string fields unconditionally. If input causes those fields to be non-NULL but invalid/non-malloc pointers, free() is invoked on attacker-influenced garbage and crashes.
